research_rationale:
EO:11681 (signed 1972-08-21; 37 FR 16909, Federal Register of August 23, 1972) revokes Executive Order No. 5221 of November 11, 1929, which limited non-official employment of officers or employees of the American Government. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing in jobs/fr-originals; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's one clause is the sole operative sentence; the text holds no other command. The revocation is a one-time command performed when the order was signed: its own text ("is hereby revoked") uses the present-tense words of immediate effect and contains no effective-date, delay or condition wording, so I read it as taking effect on signing, 1972-08-21. A performed revocation exhausts the command; that the revoked order or authority is gone is a surviving consequence, not a continuing duty of this order. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all complete, none with a coverage warning): the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, citations of the order by number in statute text and notes; edition current through 2026-10-09) recorded 0 hits; the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML recorded 0 hits; the Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (1937 onward) recorded 0 hits for this order. I also searched every held order text (the Cruden held-text search, 33118 readable files) for the order's number; the only held texts that cite it are its own Federal Register printing. I found no held order that revokes, amends or suspends it.
